$comment: Recipe for the 19 sounds the operator rendered locally before ingest. They are not reproducible from a recipe: no generator, prompt or seed was recorded, which is what separates them from the build_library.py half. Their descriptions were written from measurement (fundamental, spectral centroid, decay to -20 dB) rather than from a prompt, so nothing here claims to know what made them.

pack.name: Operator's local renders
pack.licence: Rendered locally by the operator before ingest; no third-party licence attaches. The generator and its settings were not recorded, so unlike the rest of the library these cannot be rebuilt from a recipe -- only re-ingested from the staged source file.
pack.headline: rendered locally by the operator

sounds.use: A four-second braam: the middle size between braam_soft and braam_horn. For a grave point that is not the film's gravest.
A dry two-second hit with almost no tail. The everyday accent for a card landing, where impact_soft would ring.
A high bell around 1 kHz. Cuts through a busy mix, so use it where bell_low_dry disappears.
A low bell struck once and damped — half a second of ring. A section mark for a contemplative film, where a UI chime would be wrong.
The same low bell left to ring for two seconds. For the end of a chapter rather than the start of one.
A struck chime bar near 1.6 kHz. Bright and tuned — for a figure resolving or a small good thing happening.
The glassier chime bar: same pitch, more air above it. Sits over narration without masking it.
The longest gong: over a second of decay. Give it silence on either side or it reads as noise.
The middle gong. For a transition in a film about practice, ritual or slowness.
A small gong, under a second of decay. The gentlest of the three — a beat, not a full stop.
A bright kalimba pluck. Warmer than success_chime and unmistakably played rather than designed.
The low kalimba, ringing for a second and a half. The one that can carry a section change on its own.
A mid-register kalimba note around 525 Hz. Retrigger it for a sequence of points appearing.
A struck singing bowl around 540 Hz. Calm, tuned, and long enough to sit under a fade.
The same bowl held for nearly two seconds. For an ending, or for silence that needs a floor under it.
A low bowl near 130 Hz — felt more than heard on small speakers. Check it on something with bass response.
A digital tear across a cut. Use where the picture itself glitches; over a clean cut it reads as a mistake.
The comic full stop: everything halts. One per film at most, and only in a film with a sense of humour.
A two-second bright build into a reveal. Brighter and more insistent than riser_short — for a statistic that is meant to land hard.
